memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Take a census of the whole Israelite community by their clans and families, listing every man by name, one by one. You and Aaron are to count according to their divisions all the men in Israel who are twenty years old or more and are able to serve in the army. - Num 1:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God asks Moses to count His people — not as a faceless crowd, but "every man by name, one by one." This is not a cold bureaucratic exercise. Behind every number is a name, and behind every name is a person God knows.

It is easy to feel like just one more face in a large world — one more worker, one more student, one more person in a crowded city. But God does not deal with us in bulk. He counts us individually. He knows our names. The census here was to prepare Israel for the journey ahead and for the challenges they would face; God wanted to know who was ready to stand and serve.

There is dignity in being counted by God. You are not a statistic to Him. Jesus later said that even the hairs of our head are numbered (Matt 10:30), and that He knows His sheep by name (John 10:3).

Today, if you feel overlooked or unnoticed, remember this: the God of the universe counts you one by one. He sees you. He knows exactly who you are and where you are. And in Christ, He has called you by name to belong to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you truly believe God knows you by name?
- How does being "counted" by God change how you see yourself?
- Who around you might need to be reminded that they matter to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I am never just a number to You. You know my name and You know my heart. Help me to live today as someone truly seen by You. Amen.
